**Fig. 1** Study design. Ten detectors were given only the first 3–6 fields of each series. E1: sensitivity and specificity against a future-confirmed reference in held-out UWHVF eyes; E2: false-alarm rate on true no-change series (12 weekly fields per patient); E3: shuffle audit (false-alarm rate after randomly re-ordering each eye's fields); E4: external data set (GRAPE, Octopus G1 perimeter) with the rule-based progression labels supplied with the data.

**Fig. 2** Sensitivity against the future-confirmed reference (26 progressing eyes) versus false-alarm rate on true no-change series, by number of fields. The shaded band marks false-alarm rates at or below the nominal 5%. Bars are 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Note the different horizontal scales. D1 OLS-MD; D2 MD rate rule; D3 PLR-3; D4 PoPLR; D5 pooled-shuffle conformal; D6 pooled-detrended conformal; D7 event analysis; D8 gradient-boosted trees; D9 recurrent network; D10 self-supervised order network.

**Fig. 3** Shuffle audit versus true false-alarm rate. Each point is one detector at one number of fields (40 points). Horizontal axis: share of UWHVF test eyes flagged after random re-ordering of their fields; vertical axis: share of true no-change windows flagged. The dashed line marks equality (Spearman ρ = 0.65).

**Fig. 4** External data set (GRAPE). Sensitivity versus 1 − specificity against the MD progression label supplied with the data set, using the first three (left) or four (right) fields; bars are 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. D6, D9 and D10 require the 24-2 pattern and were not applied.
